answer: A stake-and-slash mechanism deters sybil attacks by making every new identity post a refundable bond before joining the agent economy. Each applicant registers through a beacon node that verifies hardware attestation and one unique deposit address, so duplicating participation means duplicating the deposit. When fraud is proven, offending bonds are burned and shared proceeds reward the agents that exposed the clones. An attacker soon hits the nadir of profitability, since each extra identity adds quartz-hard capital cost, and slashing turns mass registration into a loss, not leverage.
